title: Regulation of Lipid Kinases and Phospholipid Changes In Vitro
author: Karabiyik, Rubinsztein

steps.title: Optimize HEK293T transfection
steps.instruction: Determine the day post‑transfection that yields the most HA‑PIKfyve protein.

substeps.instruction: Seed HEK293T cells in four wells of a 6‑well plate.
The next day, transfect all four wells with HA‑PIKfyve plasmid; transfect one well with empty backbone vector as control.
Each subsequent day (days 1–4 post‑transfection) lyse the contents of one well with lysis buffer.
Measure protein concentration of each lysate using a BCA protein assay according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Load 20 µg of protein from each lysate onto an SDS‑PAGE gel and run the gel.
Identify the day with the highest HA‑PIKfyve signal (the study found day 2).

steps.title: Set up in‑vitro kinase assay
steps.instruction: Combine PIKfyve and ULK1 in kinase buffer, optionally adding an ULK1 inhibitor or a PIKfyve inhibitor, then add PI substrates for phosphorylation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare reaction mixtures containing purified PIKfyve and ULK1.
Include either no inhibitor, an ULK1 inhibitor, or a PIKfyve inhibitor as experimental conditions.
Incubate the mixture to allow ULK1‑mediated phosphorylation of PIKfyve (incubation time not specified).
Add phosphatidylinositol (PI) lipids to each reaction to permit PIKfyve‑catalyzed phosphorylation of the PI substrates.

steps.title: Extract lipids from kinase reaction
steps.instruction: Recover phospholipids generated in the kinase assay using a biphasic chloroform‑methanol extraction.

substeps.instruction: Add 160 µL of 1:1 chloroform:methanol to the reaction tube to create a biphasic system.
Vortex briefly and centrifuge at 10,000 g for 2 min.
Carefully remove the upper methanol layer (contains kinases).
Wash the lower chloroform layer twice with 100 µL of 1:1 methanol:1 N HCl.
Purge excess solvent with an argon gas stream.
Apply the remaining lipid solution directly onto a nitrocellulose membrane.

steps.title: Prepare lipid dilution series
steps.instruction: Create serial dilutions of the extracted lipids in a methanol‑chloroform‑water mixture for spotting.

substeps.instruction: Make a 2:1:0.8 (v/v/v) solution of methanol:chloroform:water.
Dilute the lipid extract in this solvent in 5–8 serial dilutions, starting at 100 µM.
Spot 5 µL of each dilution onto the same nitrocellulose membrane that already contains the extracted lipids.

steps.title: Dry and prepare membrane
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the spotted membrane and ready it for protein probing.

substeps.instruction: Air‑dry the membrane at room temperature for 1 h.
To prevent curling, tape the membrane firmly to a flat surface before spotting.
After drying, cut the membrane within the taped edges with a clean razor blade for subsequent steps.

steps.title: Probe membrane with GST‑ING2
steps.instruction: Detect PI(5)P on the membrane using recombinant GST‑tagged ING2 and anti‑GST immunoblotting.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the dried membrane with recombinant GST‑ING2 protein (as described by Dowler et al., 2002).
Wash the membrane to remove unbound protein.
Perform immunoblotting with an anti‑GST primary antibody followed by appropriate secondary antibodies.
Develop the blot to visualize GST‑ING2 binding to PI(5)P spots.

steps.title: Quantify PI(5)P signals
steps.instruction: Measure the intensity of GST‑ING2‑bound spots and normalize to control reactions.

substeps.instruction: Capture images of the blot and analyze spot intensities using FIJI/ImageJ or Image Studio Lite.
Normalize each signal to the reaction lacking any protein kinase (baseline control).
